page.query: What should a community moderation and governance model include?
page.title: Community Moderation and Governance Model Checklist
page.description: A practical checklist for building a community moderation and governance model, covering rules, roles, escalation, tools and review cadence.
page.h1: What should a community moderation and governance model include?
page.definition: A community moderation and governance model is a documented framework that defines acceptable behaviour, moderator authority, escalation paths, response expectations, privacy boundaries, conflict handling and ongoing review cadence for an online community.
page.quick_answer: Start with a written code of conduct, assign named moderators with clear powers, set response-time targets for each severity tier, define escalation steps up to platform bans, and schedule a monthly review of metrics and policy gaps.

sections.h2: What rules and behavioural expectations should be documented?

blocks.p: A code of conduct must be specific enough that a new member can read it and know exactly what will get a warning versus a ban.

ul: Harassment, hate speech and doxxing definitions with examples
Self-promotion limits and where promotional posts belong
Intellectual property and screenshot sharing rules
Language and tone standards for each channel
Consequences ladder from verbal warning to permanent removal

sections.h2: How are moderator roles, powers and coverage defined?

blocks.p: Every moderator needs a written mandate that states what they can do without asking and what requires a second opinion.

ul: Named lead moderator and backup for each time zone
Authority to mute, delete, suspend or ban with documented thresholds
Access to moderation logs and private message review when policy allows
On-call rotation with handoff notes in a shared workspace
Quarterly training on platform updates and legal obligations

sections.h2: What escalation paths and response-time targets apply?

blocks.p: Escalation tiers turn vague complaints into measurable service levels that moderators and members can both track.

sections.h2: Which privacy boundaries and data-handling rules are required?

blocks.p: Governance must state what member data moderators can see, how long logs are kept and when law enforcement requests override community privacy.

ul: Moderator access limited to public content plus reported messages only
Retention schedule: moderation logs kept ninety days, then anonymised
Process for data-subject access requests from members
Encryption standard for exported reports and backups
Clear notice to members at join about data use and moderation visibility

sections.h2: How are conflicts of interest and appeals handled?

blocks.p: A fair model gives members a path to challenge decisions without creating moderator burnout.

ol: Member submits appeal through a dedicated form, not a public channel
Appeal reviewed by a moderator who did not take the original action
Decision documented with evidence references and communicated within forty-eight hours
Second appeal goes to community manager or external advisor if the first appeal is upheld
Final decision logged in the moderation tracker with outcome tag

sections.h2: What review cadence keeps the model current?

blocks.p: Monthly reviews catch policy drift before it becomes a crisis and give moderators a forum to propose changes.

ul: Metrics dashboard: volume by severity, median response time, appeal rate, repeat offender count
Policy gap log: situations where the code of conduct was silent or ambiguous
Tool audit: new platform features that change moderation capabilities
Moderator wellness check: workload, burnout signals, coverage gaps
Action items assigned with owners and due dates for next review

faq.q: How do I choose between volunteer and paid moderators?
faq.a: Volunteer moderators work for passion-driven communities under twenty thousand members with low risk; paid moderators are justified when coverage hours exceed twenty per week, legal exposure is high or response-time targets are contractual.

faq.q: What tools support the governance model day to day?
faq.a: Common platforms include Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups; moderation dashboards such as ModTools, AutoMod or native platform logs handle queue management, while Asana or Monday.com track escalation tickets and review tasks.

faq.q: When should legal counsel review the model?
faq.a: Engage counsel before launch if the community collects personal data, operates in regulated industries, allows user-generated content that could infringe copyright, or plans to share data with third parties; schedule an annual re-review after any policy change.

faq.q: How do I measure whether the governance model is working?
faq.a: Track median first-response time by severity, appeal overturn rate, repeat-offender percentage, moderator coverage gaps and member sentiment scores from quarterly surveys; a healthy model shows declining high-severity volume and stable or improving response times.
